transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Honestly, I'm here because I've been having a really hard time lately with listening to people when they're talking directly to me. It feels like my mind just drifts off, even when I'm trying my best to pay attention to what they are saying.

Have you had trouble paying attention like this since childhood, or did it start more recently? If it started recently, was there a particular stressor or did it come along with feeling depressed or anxious?

I've actually struggled with this since I was a kid, definitely before I turned 12. It didn't start because of recent stress or anxiety, though it has become much more of a noticeable problem for me over the last year and eight months.
Do these attention problems cause difficulties in at least two areas of your life, like at work or school and at home or in relationships? Can you give an example?

I haven't really thought about it in terms of specific areas like work or home. To be honest, I'm not entirely sure and haven't paid close attention to how it impacts those different domains specifically.

Besides drifting off when people are talking, do you often make careless mistakes, have trouble organizing tasks, lose things, forget appointments, or avoid tasks that require sustained mental effort?

I definitely lose important things all the time, like my keys, wallet, or phone. However, I don't really experience the other things you mentioned, like making careless mistakes, struggling with organization, or avoiding tasks that require a lot of mental effort.
Do you also often forget daily tasks or appointments, get easily distracted by things around you, or have trouble following through on instructions even when you understand them?

I get easily distracted by almost anything around me, whether it's a background noise, someone walking past, or even just my own random thoughts. However, I don't really struggle with forgetting appointments or following through on instructions.
Can you tell me whether these attention and distraction problems have clearly caused trouble in two different settings, such as at work or school and also at home or in relationships?
I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about whether these issues clearly cause trouble in two different settings like work and home.
When you were in school as a child, did these attention problems lead to issues like teachers saying you weren’t listening, getting distracted in class, or forgetting homework?

Yes, absolutely. My teachers back then would constantly complain that I wasn't listening to them when they spoke to me directly. I was also incredibly easily distracted by anything happening in the classroom, like someone tapping a pencil or looking out the window.
Can you give one specific recent example of how your attention problems caused trouble at work or school, and one example at home or in a relationship?

At work, I constantly get sidetracked by background noises or my own unrelated thoughts, which makes it really hard to finish my tasks on time. At home, my partner gets very frustrated with me because I often don't seem to be listening at all when they are speaking directly to me.
Do you also tend to feel restless, fidget a lot, talk excessively, interrupt others, or act impulsively, or is the problem mainly inattention?

It's actually both; besides the attention issues, I definitely struggle with hyperactivity and impulsivity as well. I find it really hard to do leisure activities quietly, and I often blurt out answers before someone has even finished speaking. I also have a very difficult time waiting my turn in most situations.
When you were a child, did you also have these hyperactive or impulsive behaviors, like being unable to stay seated, running around, blurting things out, or interrupting others?

Yes, those behaviors definitely started when I was a kid, well before I turned 12. I distinctly remember always blurting out answers before people could even finish speaking and constantly struggling to wait my turn. I also had a really hard time just playing or doing activities quietly back then.
